candidate.answerReason: The semicircular route is π/2 times as long as the straight stretch. Dividing π/2 miles by 5 miles per hour gives π/10 hours, matching B.

methods.label: Compare each arc with its diameter
methods.explanation:
There is no need to count the semicircles. Each one has the same ratio of curved distance to forward distance along the highway.

For a semicircle with diameter \(d\), its full circle has circumference \(\pi d\), so the semicircular arc has length \(\pi d/2\). Meanwhile, that arc advances Robert along the highway by its diameter, \(d\).

The successive diameters span the one-mile stretch, so replacing those straight distances with semicircular arcs multiplies the total distance by \(\pi/2\). Robert therefore rides \(\pi/2\) miles. Using time equals distance divided by speed gives
\[
\text{time}=\frac{\pi/2}{5}=\frac{\pi}{10}\text{ hours}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\pi/10}\) hours, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Half of a circle's circumference and the distance-speed-time relationship give an elementary AMC 8 solution.
